title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook (Comprehensive v8)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This playbook defines Redwood Inference's on-call and incident response processes, runbook structure, postmortem requirements, on-call rotations, game day guidance, and templates for status page updates and customer communications. The goal is to enable predictable, fast, and consistent incident handling that minimizes customer impact and ensures post-incident learning.

Scope

- Applies to all production-facing services and control plane systems (hosted API, dedicated control plane, private deployment orchestration, telemetry pipelines).
- Excludes purely experimental branches and non-production testbeds unless explicitly marked as on-call-critical.

Principles

1. Safety first: protect customer data and preserve service integrity.
2. Fastest path to mitigation is primary; root cause analysis comes after service restoration.
3. Clear ownership and escalation reduce time-to-resolution.
4. Blameless postmortems: focus on systemic fixes and follow-ups.

Incident lifecycle (high-level)

1. Detection and Triage
   - Sources: automated alerts (PagerDuty), customer reports (support), observability triggers (Grafana), status page monitoring.
   - First responder acknowledges within SLO: 5 minutes for Sev1, 15 minutes for Sev2.
2. Mobilize
   - Identify Incident Commander (IC) and primary responder. Open an incident channel (Slack #inc-<id>) and create an incident doc (confluence incident page).
3. Mitigate
   - Implement immediate workarounds or rollbacks to restore service. Prioritize safety and customer impact reduction.
4. Communicate
   - Post initial status to status.redwood.com and to affected customer contacts within the SLA window. Use templates below.
5. Resolve and Stabilize
   - Verify service health for 30 minutes after mitigation. Monitor for recurrences.
6. Post-incident Actions
   - Run postmortem within 72 hours (draft), publish within 7 business days with action items and owners.

Severity definitions and targets

- Sev1 (P0): Complete outage or degraded behaviour impacting >50% customers or revenue-critical endpoints. Acknowledge <5m, target MTTR <2h.
- Sev2 (P1): Major degradation impacting important features or subset of customers. Acknowledge <15m, target MTTR <6h.
- Sev3 (P2): Partial impact, minor feature loss or single-customer issue under support. Acknowledge <1 business day.

Roles and responsibilities

- Incident Commander (IC): Coordinates the response, communicates externally, decides on postmortem cadence.
- Primary Responder(s): Engineers actively debugging and implementing mitigations.
- Secondary Responder: Backup for primary ops and handles related tasks (logs, metrics).
- Communications Lead: Prepares status page updates and customer comms.
- PagerDuty Policy Owner: Maintains rotation schedules and escalation policies.
- Postmortem Owner: Ensures postmortem is written, actions tracked, and verified on closure.

Runbook structure (standard for each service)

- Title: Service name and environment (e.g., api-gateway.prod)
- Summary: 2-line description and impact surface
- Symptoms: What customers/alerts typically look like
- Detection queries: Grafana/Loki/Metric thresholds and example queries
- Immediate checks (first 10 minutes):
  1. Check primary dashboard (link).
  2. Confirm control plane health: /health endpoint and traceback logs.
  3. Verify infra: GPU node counts, autoscaler logs, database connections.
  4. Check recent deploys (CI/CD pipeline) and rollback if needed.
- Common mitigations:
  - Scale up dedicated pools: infra autoscale command (example below).
  - Re-route traffic to fallback model variant via smart routing policy.
  - Flush KV cache: specify cache keysets.
- Escalation matrix: who to page at 15m, 1h, 3h thresholds.
- Post-incident follow-ups: runbook updates, monitoring improvements, alert tuning.

Example CLI snippets (for responders)

- Check service health:
  curl -sS https://api.redwood.internal/health | jq

- Scale dedicated pool (kubectl example):
  kubectl -n redwood scale deployment dedicated-pool --replicas=10

- Rollback last deploy (CI token required):
  ./ci rollback --service api-gateway --to-revision <prev>

Incident comms templates

- Status page short update (initial):
  Title: Degraded performance for Hosted API (region us-east-1)
  Impact: Some customers may experience increased latency or truncated responses.
  Status: Investigating
  Started: 2026-02-10T09:12:00Z
  Notes: We are investigating increased tail latency in the inference runtime. Engineers are collecting traces and examining recent kernel updates.

- Status page follow-up (mitigation):
  Title: Mitigation in place — traffic rerouted to fallback variant
  Impact: Majority of customers restored; some low-volume requests may still see higher latency.
  Status: Mitigated
  Started: 2026-02-10T09:12:00Z
  Updated: 2026-02-10T10:04:00Z
  Next update: In 30 minutes or when full recovery confirmed

- Customer email template (initial):
  Subject: Incident: Degraded API performance in us-east-1

  Hi <Customer Name>,

  We’re writing to let you know we are investigating increased latency affecting the Hosted API in us-east-1. Our on-call team is actively working to identify the root cause and apply a mitigation. We will provide an update within 30 minutes or when we have a material change.

  Impact: Some requests may return with higher latency or truncated responses.

  Next steps: We will send a mitigation update as soon as we have one. If this is causing critical business impact, reply to this message and our support team will prioritize your ticket.

  Thank you for your patience,
  Redwood Inference Support

Postmortem process and template

- Timeline: Create draft within 72 hours, include preliminary findings and immediate action items. Finalize and publish within 7 business days.
- Format required (confluence incident page must include):
  - Summary (2 paragraphs)
  - Impact (customer-facing description and metrics)
  - Timeline (timestamped events)
  - Root cause (technical summary)
  - Contributing factors (systemic/process gaps)
  - Corrective actions (owner, due date, verification steps)
  - Metrics to prove fix (SLOs, error rates, latency targets)

Checklist for a complete postmortem

1. Incident doc linked to PagerDuty incident and status page entries.
2. All participants listed with roles.
3. Action items with owners and due dates.
4. No-op items pruned; duplicate items merged.
5. Follow-up verification scheduled on calendar.

On-call rotations and scheduling

- Rotation length: 1 week per engineer for primary pager duties.
- Secondary (backup) coverage: weekly rotation offset by 3 days.
- On-call leads: one rotation coordinator per quarter owns schedule and handoffs.
- Handoff process: outgoing on-call posts a short summary (open incidents, maintenance windows, ongoing mitigations) to #oncall-handoffs in Slack and updates the on-call calendar event.
- Time-off & escalation: swap requests must be submitted via PagerDuty 72 hours in advance where possible.

Game days and training

- Frequency: Quarterly game days per team (minimum 1 per quarter for core infra teams).
- Objectives: exercise incident playbooks, validate runbooks, test status page automation, and rehearse customer comms.
- Typical game day scenario: simulated Sev1 (regional outage) requiring routing failover and cross-team coordination.
- Post-game day: capture lessons, update runbooks, and track action items in backlog.

Operational tooling and dashboards

- Primary dashboards: Service Health (SLO & error budget), Latency P95/P99 per route, Pod/Node resource utilization, Queue backpressure metrics.
- Alerting thresholds (examples):
  - API error rate >1% sustained for 3m => P1
  - P99 latency > 2s for 5m => P1
  - Autoscaler failing to provision GPUs => P0

Maintenance windows and planned work

- Communicate planned maintenance at least 72 hours prior on the status page and to affected customers.
- During maintenance, on-call duty remains active for regression detection; create dedicated monitoring rules for the window.

RCA follow-ups and verification

- Owners must set a verification test for each corrective action. Verification can be a targeted game day, alert removal, or metric stabilization for 7 days.
- Postmortem owner marks action item closed only after verification evidence is attached to the incident doc.

Appendix: Quick reference templates

- Slack incident channel naming: #inc-<YYYYMMDD>-<short-service>-<sevid>
- Incident doc naming: Incident - <YYYY-MM-DD> - <service> - Sev<1|2|3>

- Quick checklist for first responder:
  1. Acknowledge PagerDuty and set response timer.
  2. Open Slack channel and incident confluence doc.
  3. Run immediate checks (health, deploys, infra).
  4. Apply safe mitigation or rollback.
  5. Notify Communications Lead for status update.

- Example status page public timeline entry (postmortem summary):
  10:04 UTC — Mitigation applied: traffic rerouted to fallback model variants.
  10:45 UTC — Verified recovery across all zones; monitoring shows latency within normal bounds.
  11:30 UTC — Postmortem published: https://confluence.redwood/incident/2026-02-10-api-latency

Contacts and ownership
